questions.solution:
${T}_{1} = K\left(l - {l}_{1}\right)$

${T}_{2} = K ( l - {l}_{2} )$

So, $\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{1} - l}{{l}_{2} - l}$

$∴ {T}_{1}l - {T}_{1}{l}_{2} = {T}_{2}l - {T}_{2}{l}_{1}$

Hence, final length $= l + {l}^{'}$

                               $= 5a - 4a + 9a - 9a$

                          ${l}_{0} = 5b - 4a$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The density of water at the surface of ocean is $ρ$. If the bulk modulus of water is $B$, then the density of ocean water at depth, when the pressure is $\alpha{p}_{0}$ where ${p}_{0}$& is the atmospheric pressure, is
questions.solution:
From the definition of bulk modulus

$\text{B} = - \dfrac{\text{dp}}{\dfrac{\text{dV}}{\text{V}}}$

As we move from surface to place where pressure changes to $\alpha {p}_{0}$, let us assume volume changes by $\Delta \text{V}$, then

$\text{B} = - \dfrac{\text{V} \Delta \text{p}}{\Delta \text{V}} = \dfrac{\text{V} \left(\alpha - 1\right) {p}_{0}}{\Delta \text{V}}$

New volume, $V^{′} = \text{V} - \Delta \text{V} = \left[1 - \dfrac{\left(\alpha - 1\right) {p}_{0}}{\text{B}}\right] V$

Density at the given depth, ${ρ}^{′} = ρ \dfrac{\text{V}}{V^{′}}$, where $ρ$ is density at surface

${ρ}^{′} = \dfrac{ρ \times \text{B}}{\text{B} - \left(\alpha - 1\right) {p}_{0}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If Young's modulus of the material is three times of its modulus of rigidity, then its volume elasticity will be
questions.solution:
Since, we know,

$Y = 2η \left($1 + $\sigma\right) ...(i)

Where, $Y =$ Young's modulus and $η =$ modulus of rigidity.

Given, $Y = 3η$

From Equation (i), we get

$3η = 2η $\left(1 + \sigma\right)$

$⇒ 1 + \sigma = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ \sigma = 1 / 2$

$∴$ Bulk modulus, $K = \dfrac{Y}{3 ( 1 - 2\sigma )}$

Thus, $K = \dfrac{Y}{3\left(1 - 2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{Y}{3 ( 1 - 1 )} = \infty$

Thus, volume elasticity is infinity.

questions.q: A given quantity of an ideal gas is at pressure $P$ and absolute temperature $T$. The isothermal bulk modulus of the gas is
questions.solution:
In the isothermal process

PV = constant

$∴ \text{P}\text{d}\text{V} + \text{V}\text{d}\text{P} = 0$ or $\left(\dfrac{\text{d}\text{P}}{\text{d}\text{V}}\right) = - \left(\dfrac{P}{V}\right)$

$∴$~Bulk modulus, $\text{B} = - \left(\dfrac{\text{d}\text{P}}{\text{d}\text{V} / \text{V}}\right) = - \left(\dfrac{\text{d}\text{P}}{\text{d}\text{V}}\right)\text{V}$

$∴ \text{B} = - \left[\left(- \dfrac{P}{V}\right)\text{V}\right] = \text{P}$

$∴ \text{B} = \text{P}$

questions.solution:
Let the original length be $l$.

In first case,

${l}_{1} = l + d{l}_{1}$

Using Hooke's law, $x = \dfrac{T}{K}$

Where, $x$ is the displacement.

We have, ${l}_{1} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{K}$... (i)

Similarly, ${l}_{2} = l + \dfrac{{T}_{2}}{K}$... (ii)

Solving Equations. (i) and (ii), we get

$l = \dfrac{{l}_{1}{T}_{2} - {l}_{2}{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}$

questions.q: Two wires& $A$ and $B$ are of the same materials. Their lengths are in the ratio $1: 2$ and diameters are in the ratio $2: 1$ . When stretched by force ${F}_{A}$ and ${F}_{B}$ respectively, they get an equal increase in their lengths. Then the ratio $\dfrac{FA}{FB}$ should be
questions.solution:
Force $F = \dfrac{YA ∆ l}{l}$

Substituting area $A = π{\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{π{d}^{2}}{4}$

So, we have $F = \dfrac{Yπ{d}^{2} ∆ l}{4l}$

$F ∝ \dfrac{{d}^{2} ∆ l}{l} \left[∵ \dfrac{Yπ}{4} = constant\right]$

Hence, using equation (i), we have

${F}_{A} ∝ \dfrac{{d}_{A}^{2} ∆ {l}_{A}}{{l}_{A}}$ ...(i)

${F}_{B} ∝ \dfrac{{d}_{B}^{2} ∆ {l}_{B}}{{l}_{B}}$ ...(ii)

Form equations (i) and (ii), we get

$∴ \dfrac{{F}_{A}}{{F}_{B}} = \dfrac{{d}_{A}^{2} ∆ {l}_{A}}{{l}_{A}} × \dfrac{{l}_{B}}{{d}_{B}^{2} ∆ {l}_{B}}$

As $∆ {l}_{A} = ∆ {l}_{B} = ∆ l$

Therefore $\dfrac{{F}_{A}}{{F}_{B}} = \dfrac{{d}_{A}^{2}}{{d}_{B}^{2}} × \dfrac{{l}_{B}}{{l}_{A}}$

Putting $\dfrac{{d}_{A}}{{d}_{B}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

And $\dfrac{{l}_{B}}{{l}_{A}} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

We get ${F}_{A}: {F}_{B} = 8: 1$

questions.q: The length of elastic string, obeying Hooke's law is ${l}_{1}$ metres when the tension $4N$ and ${l}_{2}$ metres when the tension is $5N$. The length in metres when the tension is $9N$ is
questions.solution:
Let ${l}_{0}$ be the unstretched length and ${l}_{3}$ be the length under a tension of 9 N. Then

$Y = \dfrac{4{l}_{0}}{A( {l}_{1} - {l}_{0} )} = \dfrac{5{l}_{0}}{A( {l}_{2} - {l}_{0} )}$

$= \dfrac{9{l}_{0}}{A( {l}_{3} - {l}_{0} )}$

These give $\dfrac{4}{{l}_{1} - {l}_{0}} = \dfrac{5}{{l}_{2} - {l}_{0}} ⇒ {l}_{0} = 5{l}_{1} - 4{l}_{2}$

Further, $\dfrac{4}{{l}_{1} - {l}_{0}} = \dfrac{9}{{l}_{3} - {l}_{0}}$

Substituting the value of ${l}_{0}$ and solving, we get ${l}_{3} = 5{l}_{2} - 4{l}_{1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An iron wire AB has& diameter of $\text{0}\text{.6 mm}$ and length $\text{3 m}$ at ${0}^{∘} \text{C}$.The wire is now stretched between the opposite walls of a brass casing at ${0}^{∘} \text{C}$. What is the extra tension that will be set up in the wire when the temperature of the system is raised to ${40}^{∘} \text{C}$?

Given ${α}_{brass} = 18 \times {10}^{– 6} / \text{K}$

${α}_{iron} = 12 \times {10}^{– 6} / \text{K}$

${Y}_{iron} = 21 \times {10}^{10} {\text{N/m}^{2}$


&
questions.solution:
Increase in length of the iron wire $= \text{L} \alpha \Delta \text{t} = \text{L} \times \text{12} \times {10}^{- 6} \times \text{40} = \text{48L} \times {10}^{- 5} m$

Increase in length of the brass tube $= \text{L} \alpha \Delta \text{t} = \text{L} \times \text{18} \times {10}^{- 6} \times \text{40} = \text{72L} \times {10}^{- 5} m$

Since the increase in length of the brass tube is greater than that of the iron wire, the latter will be tightened. Let T be the tension in the wire. Then

$\text{Stress} = \dfrac{T ⁡}{\pi {r ⁡}^{2}} = \dfrac{T ⁡}{\pi {\left(3 \times 1 {0}^{- 4}\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{T ⁡}{9 \pi \times 1 {0}^{- 8}}$

$\text{Strain} = \dfrac{\left(7 2 L ⁡ - 4 8 L ⁡\right) \times 1 {0}^{- 5}}{L ⁡} = 2 4 \times 1 {0}^{- 5}$

$\text{Since stress} = Y \times \text{strain}\text{,}\dfrac{T ⁡}{9\pi \times 1{0}^{- 8}} = 21 \times 1{0}^{10} \times 24 \times 1{0}^{- 5}$

$\text{T} = 2 1 \times 1 {0}^{10} \times 2 4 \times 1 {0}^{- 5} \times 9 \pi \times 1 {0}^{- 8} = \text{14.2 N}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Bulk modulus for an incompressible liquid is
questions.solution:
The Bulk modulus is given by

$B = - \dfrac{pV}{∆ V}$

If liquid is incompressible, so

$∆ V = 0$

$Hence, B = - \dfrac{pV}{0} = \infty ⟹ B = \infty ( infinity )$

questions.q: Two wires having the same length and material are stretched by the same force. Their diameters are in the ratio $1: 3$. The ratio of strain energy per unit volume for these two wires (smaller to larger diameter), when stretched, is
options:
$3: 1$
&
questions.solution:
Strain energy per unit volume $u = \dfrac{U}{V} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times stress \times strain$

$\dfrac{U}{V} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{F}{A} \times \dfrac{∆ l}{l}$

$\dfrac{U}{V} = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{Stress} \times \dfrac{\text{Stress}}{Y}$

$∴ \dfrac{{u}_{S}}{{u}_{L}} = \dfrac{{Y}_{L}}{{Y}_{S}} \times {( \dfrac{Strain( S )}{\text{Stress}( S )} )}^{2} = {( \dfrac{{A}_{L}}{{A}_{S}} )}^{2}$

$= {( \dfrac{{r}_L^{2}}{{r}_S^{2}} )}^{2} = ( \dfrac{81}{1} )$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A metal rod of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is heated through $T ° C$. What is the force required to prevent the expansion of the rod lengthwise?
$[Y$ = Young's modulus of the material of rod, $\alpha =$ coefficient of linear expansion$]$
questions.solution:
$∆ L = \alphaLT$ ...... (i)

Also $Y = \dfrac{F}{A} . \dfrac{L ( 1 + \alphat )}{∆ L}$

Or $∆ L = \dfrac{F . L ( 1 + \alphat )}{A . Y}$ ........ (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii)

$\dfrac{F . L\left(1 + \alphat\right)}{A . Y} = \alphaLT$

$∴ F = \dfrac{AY\alphaT}{( 1 + \alphat )}$
